reports.title: York Space Systems Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results

guidance.heading: Business Outlook as of November 12, 2026
section: York Space Systems narrowed its guidance range for the full year 2026 to be in the range of $380 million to $400 million.

We are working on a pipeline of government opportunities worth $14.9 billion, an increase of $3 billion as compared to June 30, 2026. This analysis considers the next two years, and we only included opportunities from potential customers we have spoken to directly.

desk.headline: Revenue down 7% to $84.2m, miss, with $750m goodwill write-down; 2026 revenue range narrowed to $380–400m
results: Revenue fell 7% to $84.2m and gross margin slipped to 18% from 22%.
A $749.7m non-cash goodwill write-down, tied to uncertain timing of contract awards beyond 2026, drove a net loss of $807.4m ($5.99 a share).
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $27.6m as spending rose after acquisitions and the IPO.
Backlog was $581.0m; the identified government pipeline grew to $14.9bn from about $11.9bn in June.
Liquidity stood at $459m: $309m cash plus an undrawn $150m credit line. A deal to buy Outlook Industries was announced.

guidance.summary: York tightened its 2026 revenue range to $380–400m from $375–405m, keeping the $390m midpoint. It gives no profit guidance.

points: Large government awards have slipped later; management sees constellation decisions around mid-2027.
The impairment followed the August guidance cut and a share price below book value; no repeat is expected.
Q4 revenue should rise from Q3, but the adjusted EBITDA loss is seen slightly larger than Q3's.
Full-year gross margin is expected in the low 20s, with mid-20s a longer-term aim.
Subsidiaries are expected to exceed 20% of revenue in 2027; Outlook Industries was called a small deal.
call.source: Q3 2026 call transcript — Earnings Whispers, 12 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 2026 release (13 Aug 2026)
